transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. I guess what brings me in is... well, I just don't feel real happiness or closeness anymore. It's hard to explain, but even when my wife tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or if something goes really well at work, I just don't feel it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don't know if I would call it depressed. I mean, I don't really feel sad or... or down, exactly. It's more like what I was just saying. I just don't feel much of anything at all. It's just kind of blank.
Did this start after a major stressful event or change in your life?
Yeah, it did. Um... this has all been going on since the retrofit accident. That was about a year and seven months ago now.
Since the accident, have you had the feeling that you yourself aren’t real, or that the world around you feels unreal?

No, um... I don't think so. I know I'm real, and the world around me is real. It's not like I'm walking around in a dream or anything like that. It's just... like I said, I just feel kind of blank or disconnected from it all. But I haven't really felt like things are actually unreal, no.
Have you been feeling sad most days?
Like I said before, I wouldn't really call it sad. I don't wake up feeling down or like crying or anything. It's really just that blankness. I just feel kind of empty, not sad.
Do you still enjoy the things you used to enjoy?

Not really, no. That's actually a big part of why I'm here. I just... I don't feel any real happiness anymore. Even with things I used to like. Like, my wife tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or even if something goes really well at work... I just don't feel anything good. No happiness, no real closeness to anyone. It's just flat.
Do you have unwanted memories of the accident that keep coming back?

Yeah, I do. It doesn't take much to trigger them, either. Just... normal things at work. A standard plant alarm going off, looking over a retrofit checklist, or sometimes even just the smell of hot metal. It just... it throws me right back there. I'm right back to seeing him on the floor, hearing everyone yelling for help. It just keeps coming back.
Since the accident, have you been avoiding reminders of it?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I avoid that specific production line whenever I can. If it needs to be walked, I'll just send someone else to do it. And... if people start talking about the rollout, or the investigation into what happened, I just shut the conversation down. I just don't want to deal with it.
Since the accident, have you been feeling constantly on guard or watchful, like you can’t relax?

Yeah, definitely. I just can't seem to turn it off. When I'm out on the floor, I'm constantly checking the gauges, looking at the exits, watching people's hands... making sure I know exactly where the emergency stops are at all times. And it's not just out there, either. Even if I'm just sitting in a conference room for a meeting, I always make sure to pick a seat where I can see the door. I just can't let my guard down.
During the accident, did you believe that you or someone else might die or be seriously injured?

I'm not really sure. It all happened so fast that I don't think I had time to process it like that. I mean, I knew it was bad when I saw him on the floor, but... my brain wasn't really forming thoughts about whether he was going to die or not right in that exact moment. It was just chaos, and I was mostly just reacting to the shouting. I wasn't really thinking ahead to how bad it might be.
Did you see someone get seriously injured in the accident?

No, not the actual moment it happened. I just... I heard all the yelling first. By the time I turned around to look at the line, he was already down on the floor. So I didn't see the machinery actually hit him or anything like that, just... just what it looked like right after.
Since the accident, have you found yourself blaming yourself for what happened?

Yeah, I do. It's... I just keep thinking that I can't trust my own judgment anymore. As the manager, I'm supposed to be on top of things, and now I just feel like, if I miss even one small detail on a schedule, or maybe overlook a machine setting... somebody else is going to get hurt because of me. So, yeah, I guess I do put a lot of that on myself.
Since the accident, have you had nightmares about it?

Yeah, I do. Sleep has been... really difficult. Most nights, I just lie there in the dark, replaying the plant in my head, over and over. And then, when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I either jolt awake from dreams about the assembly line, or I just wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning. And even when I wake up, I feel like I never really rested at all.
Did the coworker you found on the floor have injuries that looked life-threatening or very severe?
No, not really. I mean, he was definitely hurt, but... it didn't look like he was going to die or anything. It was bad, but not life-threatening.
Do you believe the accident happened because of something you did or failed to do?

Yeah, I do. Like I said before, I just keep thinking that I can't trust my own judgment anymore. I mean, as the manager, I'm supposed to be the one making sure everything runs right. Now I'm just constantly worried that if I miss one little detail on a schedule, or if I don't catch a machine setting being off... somebody else is going to get hurt because of me. So, yeah, I definitely feel like it's my fault.
After the accident, did you learn that your coworker had been seriously injured?
No, I didn't. Um, like I said, it didn't look too bad at the time, and... well, I never heard anything different after the fact. I mean, from what I was told, it wasn't anything major.
Before the accident, had you ever gone through a period like this where, for at least a couple of weeks, you lost interest or pleasure in things most days?

No, I don't think so. Before the accident, things were... fine, really. I enjoyed my normal routine, liked my job, and had things I liked to do on the weekends. I never had a stretch where I just lost interest in everything for weeks at a time. That kind of thing has really only started since the accident.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, not just the accident or safety at work?

No, I don't think so. Um, my mind is pretty much just stuck on the accident and... and the safety stuff at work. I don't really sit around worrying about a bunch of other random things, like bills or everyday stuff. It's really just... it all comes back to my job and making sure I don't mess up and get somebody hurt.
At the time, did you understand that your coworker had been seriously injured?
No, I didn't. Like I said before, it really didn't look that bad when it happened. I didn't think anyone was seriously hurt at the time.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of killing yourself?

No, I haven't. I mean, things are really hard right now, and I feel awful a lot of the time, but... no, I've never thought about ending my life or anything like that. I don't want to die, I just... I just want to feel normal again.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal ideation, which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: No, I haven't. I mean, things are really hard right now, and I feel awful a lot of the time, but... no, I've never thought about ending my life or anything like that. I don't want to die, I just... I just want to feel normal again.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's main concern for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began after a clear psychosocial stressor (workplace accident) and have persisted with intrusive memories, avoidance, hypervigilance, sleep disturbance, emotional numbing/anhedonia, and guilt focused on the event. Full major depressive syndrome is not clearly established because the patient repeatedly denies persistent sadness and prior depressive episodes, and recurrent depressive disorder is not supported. PTSD-like features are present, but the interview does not confirm a qualifying life-threatening or severely injurious trauma exposure as required for PTSD, making adjustment disorder the best fit among the provided options.
